source_review.notes: Checked primary failure-detector, SWIM, GFS, replica-maintenance, and latent-sector-error research plus current official HDFS and Ceph heartbeat, inventory, placement-group, down/out, flapping, full-capacity, and backfill-reservation documentation. Sources support suspicion, membership, block reports, safe startup, topology-aware repair, transient-failure grace, bounded recovery, and corruption claims. All ten URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed expected, observed, and verified replica sets; replication deficit; coded erasure margin; liveness origin; detector, grace, queue, transfer, verification, and exposure times; bytes and throughput.
Checked node incarnation, report sequence, membership epoch, placement epoch, object generation, repair identity, and failure domains are separately named.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Suspicion evidence, authoritative membership, desired placement, observed inventory, verified protection, and physical repair remain distinct.

evidence: Executed repair-exposure-accounting with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced 687,194,767,360 repair bytes, 8,192 seconds transfer, 8,507 seconds exposure, and 141.8 minutes.
Recomputed 120 TiB at 2 GiB/s as 61,440 seconds or 17.07 hours and replica readable-copy margins as two, one, and two.
Recomputed exercise one as 16,384 seconds transfer and 17,124 seconds total modeled exposure, equal to 285.4 minutes or about 4.757 hours.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The calculations use constant effective throughput and explicitly omit queueing, contention, coding fan-in, verification, tail skew, and further faults where appropriate.

evidence: Derived exposure as the sum of detection, grace, queue, transfer, and verification/registration intervals under a declared time origin.
Derived ideal transfer duration as bytes divided by sustained effective throughput and checked unit conversions.
Checked replication deficit and MDS erasure margin formulas while retaining failure-domain and fragment-validity qualifications.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Aggregate backlog time is not used as proof of per-object completion or durability.

evidence: Reviewed process death, pause, disk stall, event-loop overload, packet loss, asymmetric partition, observer-domain failure, flapping, restart/incarnation, stale reports, and controller failover.

Reviewed exact-k coded state, same-rack replicas, corrupt/disagreeing sources, target-full, placement change during repair, crash before registration, returning copies, safe-mode startup, maintenance, and decommission.
Reviewed forged/replayed reports, repair denial of service, tenant/residency/key policy, legal holds, archive return, sensitive telemetry, and regulated recovery.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The workflow preserves ambiguity until independent evidence and authoritative decisions justify stronger states.

evidence: Traced reporter diversity, membership authority, inventory completeness, version/profile/integrity checks, topology-valid target selection, reservation, idempotent transfer, verification, registration, and cleanup order.
Checked that no stale or corrupt copy counts toward protection and that repair cannot resurrect deleted or superseded generations.
Checked startup and returning-node reconciliation cannot trigger destructive action from incomplete inventories.
invariant_checking.notes: Bytes copied is an intermediate state; policy is restored only after verified authoritative registration.

evidence: Reviewed all ten detector-and-repair audit obligations from observation and authority through inventory, risk, source/target selection, transfer, feedback, and correlated-fault testing.

Checked counterexamples for no-heartbeat-equals-dead, shortest-timeout-equals-safe, report-equals-authority, observed-count-equals-protection, down-equals-out, bytes-arrived-equals-repaired, empty-node-equals-target, maximum-bandwidth-equals-safe, timer-equals-safe-mode, and responsive-equals-intact claims.
Reviewed repair state-machine, epoch fencing, crash-candidate reconciliation, returning-media, and exposure-model proof boundaries.
proof_review.notes: Detector accuracy, membership safety, data integrity, durability, performance, security, and governance require distinct evidence.

evidence: Audited uses of failed, dead, current, authoritative, complete, valid, verified, protected, safe, recoverable, and prove.
Confirmed fixture outputs are labeled simple exposure and backlog models rather than production failure probabilities, completion objectives, or topology proofs.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Product terms such as down, out, recovery, and backfill are explicitly scoped because implementations differ.

evidence: Reviewed retrieval dates, heartbeat/probe distributions, false positives, detection tails, outage durations, report lag, topology, margins, queue age, repair throughput/tails, foreground impact, and fault injection.
Confirmed no universal timeout, optimal grace, production durability, repair objective, regulatory approval, certification, or external-review claim is made.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production claims require exact detector implementation, workload, topology, fault correlation, integrity evidence, capacity state, repair controls, and repeated recovery observations.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed observation, detector evidence, incarnation and membership, inventories, protection states, repair workflow, grace, source/target selection, recovery/backfill, prioritization, feedback, startup, maintenance, corruption, security, and evidence as one coherent model.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed heartbeats and peer reports, down/out separation, report continuity, safe mode, risk classes, repair reservations, per-domain throttles, flapping controls, return-to-service, decommission, telemetry, fault injection, and archival recovery. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from epistemic limits through authoritative repair and operations; ten examples and five complete answers cover observer partitions, grace, margins, crash recovery, flapping, startup, backlog, source choice, decommission, and regulated archives.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external failure-detector researcher, distributed-storage operator, storage vendor, security auditor, records authority, archive custodian, research-ethics body, or certification review is claimed.
